summary: Franz Bopp worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, and at Paris, London, and Göttingen. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1838–1840) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1839–1841). He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and Oxford (~1848–1854) as professor of modern languages.

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866) and as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Göttingen (~1881–1908).
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist. He completed master's studies at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned a PhD from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1988–1993) and was professor at Munich (2006–2012).
François Gros was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1957) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).
François Jacob studied at Lycée Carnot and the Paris Medical Faculty (~1937–1947). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1964 to 1991.

Françoise Pommaret works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at INALCO and the University of Paris. Her career includes serving as Directeur de recherche at CNRS (2002), lecturer at INALCO, and advisor at the College of Language and Culture Studies (~2007).
Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied under Heather Stoddard (~1995–2003). She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~2005).
Fred Pfeil was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his education at Amherst College (~1967–1971). He held an academic post at Oregon State University.
Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Minnesota from ~1971 to 2017.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as librarian at the India Office Library (~1903–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held posts at the universities of Bergen (~1961–1972), Oslo (~1974–1985), Harvard (~1989–1997), Emory (~1989–2008), and Boston University (~1997–2009).
Friederike Assandri is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. She studied at Heidelberg University as a PhD student under Gunther-Dietz Sontheimer and later held a post there (attested 2013).

Friedhelm Hardy worked in Indology and religious studies. He held a post at King's College London (~1971–2004) and served as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Oxford (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Paris (~1953–1959) and served as Professor of Sinology at the University of Hamburg (~1976–1982).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826). He held posts as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (~1828–1831) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

Friedrich Bechtel was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at the University of Göttingen (~1873–1876). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1878–1895) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1895–1924).

Friedrich Bollensen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1860) and served as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).
